subject: Microburst + long-history billing behavior — request and proposed terms

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Microburst + long-history billing behavior — request and proposed examples

Hi Jordan / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the call today. One outstanding item before we finalize the SOW: how Redwood bills when an integration mixes high-frequency microburst streaming calls (sub-second replies) with occasional long-history retrievals (20k+ token context windows). Procurement asked for a simple, auditable description we can include in the contract.

Short version of our questions:
- How are microburst streaming calls rounded / floored for billing? Is there a per-call minimum?
- When a request hits a long-history model (e.g., 16k or 32k context), does the context floor apply per request or per-session?
- How do we handle hybrid requests that stream a short reply but reference a cached long-history context?

For context, Acme expects: ~1M streaming calls/month (average 12 tokens generated each) plus ~25k large-context retrievals (avg 8k tokens). They asked whether Redwood would apply the session minimums to each streaming call or if we can propose a blended approach that reduces initial-month overage risk.

Attached: Acme_SOW_v1.pdf (draft).

Could you confirm the official billing definitions we'd put in the SOW and whether Redwood can offer a pilot concession (e.g., waive the per-call minimum for the first 3 months or provide a microburst token discount)?

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Microburst + long-history billing behavior — Acme asks (need example invoice + concession language)

Marissa / Tessa — draft numbers below and attached a quick calc workbook (pricing_calcs.xlsx). Comments inline:

Rules (recommended, in plain language):
- Microburst streaming calls: billed per-token; rounding quantum = 10 tokens; per-call floor = 10 tokens. That keeps per-call billing predictable and keeps small overhead low.
- Long-history requests (>=8k context): context-floor = 1,024 tokens applied per individual request that triggers a new context load. If a request reuses a cached context (KV/prefix hit within 24h), we bill only the incremental tokens used to generate plus a 0 token context delta (no re-floor).
- Hybrid requests (short streamed response + referenced cached long-history): if the context is served from cache, do NOT apply the context-floor again. Only count generated tokens (rounded to quantum). If the context is loaded from cold (no cache hit), apply the context-floor once for that request.

Example month (baseline):
- Microburst calls: 1,000,000 calls x avg 12 tokens gen -> raw tokens = 12,000,000 -> rounding to quantum: 12,000,000 rounded up to nearest 10 = 12,000,000 (no change) -> billed microburst tokens = 12,000,000
- Long-history requests: 25,000 requests x avg 8,000 tokens -> raw tokens = 200,000,000 -> context-floor triggers per request = max(8,000, 1,024) so we bill 8,000 (actual) each; billed long-context tokens = 200,000,000
- Net billed tokens = 212,000,000 -> at $0.0009/token (example unit) = $190,800

Example month (peak with many cold loads):
- Assume 10% of long-history requests are cold loads that trigger context re-loads and are billed as full context + a 1,024 floor where applicable. Adjusted billed long-context tokens + microburst tokens = attach workbook for detailed step-through.

Concession options (risk & operational impact):
A) Waive per-call microburst floor (10 tokens) for first 3 months — low revenue impact for Redwood on this profile because average call is 12 tokens; operationally simple.
B) Apply 20% discount on microburst unit price for first 3 months — straightforward but impacts unit economics if volume spikes.
C) Offer a blended "burst credit pool": prepay a token credit pool that covers microburst-floor shortfalls for month 1–3; leftover credits convert to usage. More complex administratively.

Recommendation: Option A (waive per-call floor for months 1–3) is easiest and gives Acme immediate upside; it avoids changing unit pricing and preserves invoicing simplicity.

Attached: pricing_calcs.xlsx (workbook with both scenarios).

Ben Carter
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Microburst + long-history billing behavior — request and proposed examples

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Per internal discussion, here is the contract-ready language and the example math you requested.

Proposed SOW appendix (summary):
1) Billing definitions
- Microburst streaming calls: billed per generated token; rounding quantum = 10 tokens; standard per-call floor = 10 tokens (waived for first 3 months per concession below).
- Long-history context requests: billed for actual tokens consumed; a context-floor of 1,024 tokens applies only to cold context loads (i.e., when the platform loads a previously uncached context). Cached context hits (KV/prefix within 24h) do not re-trigger the context-floor.
- Hybrid calls: if the request references a cached context, only generated tokens are billed. If the request forces a cold context load, the context-floor applies once for that request.

2) Example invoice (baseline month) — see attached pricing_calcs.xlsx for worked numbers.

3) Concession (pilot) — contract clause suggestion:
"Redwood will waive the per-call microburst billing minimum (10-token floor) for the first three (3) months following service activation for Acme Health. This waiver applies only to microburst streaming calls and does not apply to long-history context loads or to charges for generated tokens."

If that sounds good I can update the SOW and send a DocuSign link. I attached an updated SOW (Acme_SOW_v2.pdf) with the appendix table.

Link to updated SOW: https://www.docusign.com/link/ACME-SOW-v2
